original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G together with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary order is exactly the cycle C.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Open Problem 30: Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form along with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary corresponds to the given Hamiltonian cycle C.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s intended problem very closely: it uses the correct input format (a graph via adjacency matrix together with a Hamiltonian cycle), asks the right decision question, targets visibility graphs of simple polygons, and requires the supplied Hamiltonian cycle to be the polygon’s boundary cycle. It is also correctly narrower than the general polygon-visibility recognition problem, because the boundary cycle is provided as part of the input.
missing_details: The draft should explicitly define what it means for G to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon: two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely within the polygon.
It should make the existence quantifier explicit: decide whether there exists some simple polygon P realizing the given data.
It should say that the polygon uses the same labeled vertex set as G, and that those vertices appear along the boundary in the cyclic order prescribed by the given Hamiltonian cycle C.

It should clarify that C is part of the input, so this is the restricted recognition problem where the boundary edges are already identified, not the separate problem of first finding the correct Hamiltonian cycle.

The paper’s wording is that the polygon boundary corresponds to the given Hamiltonian cycle; the draft’s phrase "boundary order is exactly the cycle C" is close, but it is better to phrase this as correspondence of the boundary cycle to avoid implying any extra orientation-sensitive requirement beyond the cyclic order.

The scope should remain exactly simple polygons in this prescribed-boundary recognition setting; it should not drift into the broader recognition problem, reconstruction, or the problem of recovering the boundary cycle from the graph.
refined_question: Given a simple undirected graph G = (V,E) in adjacency-matrix form and a Hamiltonian cycle C = (v1,v2,...,vn,v1) of G on the same labeled vertex set, decide whether there exists a simple polygon P whose vertices are v1,v2,...,vn in the cyclic boundary order prescribed by C and such that, for every distinct i,j, the edge vivj is in E if and only if the straight-line segment joining the corresponding vertices of P lies entirely within P; that is, whether G is the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon whose boundary corresponds to the given Hamiltonian cycle C.
justification: The exact paper target is Open Problem 30 in Section 4.1, not the broader recognition problem of Open Problem 28 and not the separate boundary-recovery problem of Open Problem 34. The local context immediately before Open Problem 30 explains that this version assumes a Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the polygon boundary is already given, which makes the problem easier than general recognition because the boundary edges are already identified. The same nearby discussion supplies the intended boundary-order setup for the labeled vertices and introduces the visibility/invisibility language used in this prescribed-boundary recognition setting. Theorem 13, stated immediately after Open Problem 30, confirms that the surrounding discussion is precisely about testing necessary conditions for this restricted recognition problem. Your draft is therefore essentially correct, but it should be made fully stand-alone by explicitly stating the visibility relation and the existence of a realizing polygon.
